Add LOO-PSIS to brma Objects

Source: R/loo.R
add_loo.brma.Rd

Compute approximate leave-one-out cross-validation (LOO-CV) using Pareto smoothed importance sampling (PSIS) for brma model objects and store the result in the object.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'brma'
add_loo(object, unit = "estimate", r_eff = NULL, parallel = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

object

a brma model object.

unit

output/deletion unit. "estimate" computes one contribution per effect-size estimate. "cluster" computes one contribution per cluster and is available only for multilevel models fitted through the specialized clustered interface.

r_eff

optional vector of relative effective sample sizes. If not provided, it is computed from the log-likelihood values.

parallel

Logical. If TRUE, loo::relative_eff() and loo::loo() use RoBMA.get_option("max_cores"). Log-likelihood construction is unchanged. If FALSE, those computations use one core.

...

additional arguments (currently ignored).

Value

The brma object with the LOO result stored in object[["loo"]][[unit]].

Details

With unit = "estimate", LOO-CV is computed with one contribution per effect-size estimate. For binomial and Poisson models, each pair of counts (ai/ci or x1i/x2i) that defines a single effect size estimate is treated as one contribution. Estimate-unit GLMM log-likelihoods integrate the nuisance base rate or log-rate over its prior: point priors and untruncated beta (base rate) and normal (log-rate) priors adaptively, other priors on a refined prior-CDF grid; a uniform(0, 1) base-rate prior is a Beta(1, 1) prior and is integrated adaptively. The grid is accepted only when its log-likelihood changes by less than 1e-6 between refinements. Any nuisance prior without an adaptive route (other than an untruncated beta base rate or an untruncated normal log-rate; truncated ones take the grid too) can fail to reach this, especially with few events or very large arms, and then stops with an error of class RoBMA_glmm_grid_nonconvergence (also of class RoBMA_glmm_numerical_error); gamma, lognormal, and inverse-gamma log-rate priors and lognormal base-rate priors are examples. A beta base-rate prior or a normal log-rate prior avoids it. When the likelihood is computed automatically after fitting (the autocompute.loo and autocompute.waic options), such a failure gives a warning and the fit is returned without LOO/WAIC; add_loo() then gives the same error.

With unit = "cluster", LOO-CV is computed with one joint contribution per cluster. For normal models without selection, weighted or not, this uses the closed-form Gaussian integral over the held-out cluster effect, with the likelihood weights applied as powers of the row densities. Cluster-unit binomial and Poisson GLMM log-likelihoods are unavailable until certified nested adaptive quadrature is implemented; use unit = "estimate" for GLMMs. Cluster-unit contributions are also unavailable for brma.mv() models, whose random-formula deletion semantics still need a dedicated design; use unit = "estimate" there.

Selection-model deletion conditions the Gaussian law on retained outcomes and on the context declared by the fitted selection model. It preserves the original publication event and selection standard errors. Product weights on retained outcomes cancel; best selection continues to depend on the best p-value among both retained and deleted outcomes. This finite-vector deletion score differs from prediction for an entirely new publication event.

For Gaussian multilevel and known-V brma.mv() models, estimate-unit LOO integrates Gaussian local effects and uses \(p(y_i \mid y_{-i}, \theta)\) within each fitted dependency block. Thus deleting one estimate retains the other estimates in its cluster or random- effect block; it does not represent prediction for a wholly new group. Gaussian brma(..., cluster = ...) models with non-unit likelihood weights also integrate the cluster effect. Their score integrates the entire powered row density against the cluster-effect distribution given the retained weighted observations, including the power-dependent normalizing constant. It is not the power of an unweighted marginal density. Earlier stored weighted estimate-unit LOO results must be recomputed with add_loo(); the fitted posterior does not need refitting for this post-fit calculation. Selection and GLMM models retain their supported routes. Numerically unresolved weighted Gaussian retained moments stop with RoBMA_weighted_gaussian_unavailable, a RoBMA_numerical_unavailable condition.

For brma.mv() models with known random-effect group covariance R, the known R matrix and fitted random-effect covariance enter the marginal \(ZGZ'\) covariance through BayesTools' compiled random-effect metadata. The same calculation applies to every supported random structure.

Estimate-unit deletion retains the fitted grouping and known-V dependency structure; it does not represent deletion of an entire new random group. Models with no local effects, sampled local effects, marginalized local effects, or a mixture of sampled and marginalized effects remain comparable when their data hash, deletion unit, retained context, and likelihood target agree. The sampled/marginalized labels are retained as provenance rather than comparison keys.

The PSIS object is essential for model comparison via loo_compare and is automatically saved in the loo result. RoBMA stores target metadata so comparisons can reject mismatched data, unit, or retained-context targets. Each finite log-likelihood column observed to be constant across posterior draws uses exact uniform importance ratios. Such columns bypass relative-ESS and generalized-Pareto fitting, including when other columns vary. Their Pareto-k diagnostic is recorded as the sentinel zero, meaning constant ratios with no tail instability rather than an estimated Pareto shape. Finite varying columns are centered by a column-specific constant before relative-ESS and PSIS evaluation. The offset is restored exactly afterward, preserving the LOO target while avoiding probability-scale underflow.

Important for model comparison: When comparing models via loo_compare, the selection is based on expected predictive performance for the documented deletion target, not in-sample fit. For dependent estimates, deleting one estimate may retain other observations from its fitted dependency block; this is not new-group prediction.

References

(Vehtari et al. 2017) (Vehtari et al. 2024)

See also

loo.brma, loo, loo_compare, pareto_k_ids

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
if (requireNamespace("metadat", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data(dat.lehmann2018, package = "metadat")
  fit <- bPET(yi = yi, vi = vi, data = dat.lehmann2018, measure = "SMD")

  fit <- add_loo(fit)
  loo_fit <- loo(fit)
  print(loo_fit)
  plot(loo_fit)
}
} # }
